title: Residence Credit on the HFIAA Surcharge — NFIP Dwelling Form Flood Policies (Write Your Own)
content:
### Residence credit — NFIP Dwelling Form Flood Policies (Write Your Own)

**Where it applies.** For a policy that carries the insured's primary-residence designation on a tier that can carry the lower surcharge while its current term was booked with the other HFIAA surcharge, on which the insured makes a renewal remittance before the term end, and only for such a policy, the current term's HFIAA surcharge is reduced by the residence credit, the credit being booked with the remittance as a re-rate credit on the current term's HFIAA surcharge line and deducted from the remittance; on every other policy, and for the Federal Policy Fee and the probation surcharge on every policy, the HFIAA surcharge, the Federal Policy Fee and the probation surcharge are booked once per term at new business or renewal and never on an endorsement.

**What it returns.** The residence credit returns the part of the current term's HFIAA surcharge above the tier's primary-residence surcharge for the part of the term the insured has lived at the insured building, because a primary residence is the home the insured lives in for more than half of the term.

- **Move date:** the date on which the insured's former home, insured with Tidemark under a HomeFlood Private Residential Flood Policies policy, was cancelled because that home was sold — the cancellation effective date of that HomeFlood policy, taking the latest such sale.
- **Surcharge gap:** the HFIAA surcharge booked for the current term less the tier's primary-residence surcharge, never below zero.

**Ladder.** The policy counts as rated as the insured's primary residence when the tier can carry the lower surcharge and the policy carries the insured's primary-residence designation.

| Situation | Residence credit |
|---|---|
| Rated as the insured's primary residence and the move took effect on or before the current term start | The whole surcharge gap |
| So rated, the move took effect after the term start, and more than half of the term's days run from the move date to the term end | The surcharge gap multiplied by the days from the move date to the term end and divided by the days of the current term, rounded half-up to the cent |
| Otherwise — no move on record, or half of the term's days or fewer remaining | No residence credit on the current term; the lower surcharge applies from the renewal |

*Hypothetical cases* (365-day term, gap 225.00 dollars). A HomeFlood sale effective before the term start: credit 225.00. A sale with 292 days left: 225.00 multiplied by 292 and divided by 365, that is 180.00. A sale with exactly 182 days left: 182 days is not more than half of 365, so no credit.
